description: A C# game engine used the way raylib is: open a window, draw each frame with plain static calls, and draw Dear ImGui in the same frame, over SDL3, Vulkan and Slang, with an ECS and source-generated behaviors underneath.
releaseNotes:
The script test's grow mode is given a minute and grows in random bytes, so its memory limit comes before its time limit on a slow runner.
The drawing leak test reads its resident baseline after the heap census it takes, and a reference frame waits until every model its scene places has loaded before it settles.
A session file that cannot be opened for a moment is read again, the puzzle's drive counts each frame a sixtieth of a second so a slow device sees its swipe, and a game that dies off Windows leaves a dump.
The strategy game's long wait in the examples job takes ten minutes to answer, and the commit with no sentence that carried a pass of this file is listed among those rule N 7.2 allows.
An entity an AnimatedModel draws gives its body the model's meshes as the clip last posed them, so a mesh or a hull collider on it makes a body where it was refused.
Light that scatters under a surface stays out of render textures and probe faces, since a render texture holds no linear frame and a probe's faces span a few pixels of a reach.
A test holds the subsurface thickness a material gives as a cap on the thickness measured, a sheet the field holds a cell thick lit through by the two millimeters given.
The commit that ignores the Voxel-Sandbox folder, whose message has no sentence, is listed among those rule N 7.2 allows.
A failed suite saves the shaders Mesa compiled, the Windows suite is held to 60 minutes, the leak test's message carries its resident series, and the macOS captures run in the pack run alone.
The voxel game has furnaces that smelt meat, sand, cobblestone, iron ore and logs over coal, charcoal and wood, iron ore in the stone with iron tools, and hearts and food outlined so they read over any color.
The voxel game leaves undrawn the sections the eye cannot see through open cells, flooding from the eye's section across the faces each section's open cells join as Minecraft's visibility graph does.
A glow light's march ends its way out of a surface where it left it, so the light past a pillar's edge rises on the wall behind without a step.
Opaque materials draw with pipelines that fold the alpha test's discard away, for the devices that turn their early depth test off under one.
The voxel game spawns zombies, skeletons, spiders and creepers in the dark in survival, which hunt the player along the blocks, strike, shoot arrows or explode, burn by day and drop their loot.
The voxel game writes a relit section's colors in place beside its packed bytes, so the light that bounces and its reference take a change of light in the frame after.
Vertex colors written in place reach the light that bounces and the reference in the frame after, the field painting again the cells a recolored mesh is nearest against its cascade's kept words and the ray scene rewriting its corners.
The voxel game opens the engine's window of the effects over the frame from its own, and its light settings read the bloom and exposure back from the engine.
Each effect over the frame is read back beside its setter, and DrawPostProcessWindow shows and sets every one in an ImGui window of its own while the picture is looked at.
The screen's probes' rays reach twice as far as the world's probes are apart where they end in the finest cascade, and a ray that went behind the depth and off the picture is handed to the field from where it stood in front, so a wall before a pillar sees it and a closed room keeps the light outside it out.
The voxel game gives the player health, food and breath in survival, hurts falls, drowning, starving and cactus, feeds the player bread, apples and raw meat, and spills the inventory at a death before a new life at the spawn.
A mesh that moved settles into the scene's field only after standing 1,024 frames, and a frame where meshes moved in their places is read by place, so walking figures that pause rebuild no cascade and cost the field a few microseconds a box.
The voxel game crafts in a grid of the inventory and at a crafting table, with wooden and stone tools that break their blocks faster and wear out, coal in the stone, and stone that drops nothing without a pickaxe.
The voxel game draws its mobs with BouncesLight off, so they keep their shadows and cost the scene field nothing as they walk.
A material's BouncesLight, true unless set, leaves a mesh that moves in most frames out of the scene's field, the glow lights and the bounce's reference while it casts its shadows.
The screen's probes find the frame before's light where each probe stood rather than by its tile's middle, a pixel off, so a still view's blend no longer drifts toward the probes to its right and below.
The voxel game plays in creative or survival mode, with an inventory, blocks that take time to break and drop what they leave, mobs that drop their loot, and stacks on the ground that the player picks up and throws.
The voxel game has pigs, cows, sheep, chickens and villagers that find their way through the blocks, run when hit, go home at night through their doors and are saved with their columns.
A probe's path-traced reference leaves out the glow of an emitter the bounce carries as a light where a path first meets it, as the probe's rays do.
Gives the GPU no colors or second texture coordinates for a mesh of positions alone, its colors kept for the light field to read.
Gives the light that bounces a guide page of its own, the radiance cascades, the field, the probes, the qualities' costs, the limits and the tools, and names it in the README.
Names the flat API's class E3D, its files, the tests' and every program's using line following, the namespace and the package as they were.
The voxel game draws its sections and clouds from positions and eight packed bytes a vertex in a stream of its own, and a relight writes the packed bytes alone.
Names the development machine's GPU in place of its model wherever a user reads, in the tests, the shaders and the guides, keeping every measurement.
Lets a mesh be uploaded from its positions alone, twelve bytes a vertex, its stream packing the rest, with every pipeline that binds a vertex reading it so.
Lets a mesh carry a vertex stream of the program's own, read as CUSTOM0 and written in place, and makes the pack wait on the examples job.
Runs the examples job from a workflow of its own, a push building every game and playing one, the pack run capturing, measuring, playing and soaking them all.
Counts the examples under the README's Examples heading and the pictures in each row of its gallery, written and checked by the examples table's script.
Gives the suite run by build/test.py an NVIDIA driver cache of its own above the driver's cap, where a full one compiled every pipeline again and failed some.
Draws a frame where no light bounces through a build of the model pass that leaves the bounce out with the glow lights, a fifth of the whole fragment stage.
Fits a capture to the gallery's size with cwebp where it is installed, so the examples job needs no ImageMagick, and names a first game step that fails.
Removes games/Pusher, Slide taking its place as the game CI builds, publishes native and plays in a window, and opens the README's guide with the cheat sheet.
title: 3DEngine
